Released at 2026-10-21

* SECURITY: **Every GitHub Actions workflow pins its actions to a full commit SHA, and a new `workflow-lint` check lints the workflow files (CI only, no runtime change).** All 171 action references that used a tag or branch now name a 40-character commit with the version as a trailing comment, expressions that were interpolated into `run:` scripts in the fuzz, load-test, badges and MinIO image workflows are passed through `env:`, and `.github/workflows/workflow-lint.yaml` runs actionlint and zizmor (pinned, checksum-verified) on every pull request and push to `main`, with the findings that exist today listed in `.github/zizmor.yml`. CodeQL also analyses the workflow files now (`Analyze (actions)`), and `scripts/ci/tests/test_workflow_action_pins.py` fails if an action reference is added without a SHA pin and version comment.
* SECURITY: **Tools installed in CI are pinned to exact versions and their downloads are verified (CI only, no runtime change).** `govulncheck`, `gosec` (and the `x/tools` it is built with) are installed at exact versions instead of `@latest`, the `gitleaks` archive is checked against a pinned SHA-256 before it is unpacked, and every `pip install` in the workflows reads a hashed lock file (`--require-hashes`, generated from a `requirements.in` next to it with `pip-compile --generate-hashes`) in place of unpinned or version-only requirements. `scripts/ci/tests/test_ci_tool_pins.py` fails if a moving tool ref, an unverified download, a pipe into a shell, an unhashed `pip install` or an `npm install` is added; the few exceptions are listed, each with its reason, in `scripts/ci/tool_pins_allowlist.txt`.
* SECURITY: **Container images used by the test stacks and CI are pinned by digest (CI and test tooling only; no change to image versions or runtime behaviour).** The images of the Compose stacks, the S3 compatibility job, the MinIO build Dockerfiles and the benchmark, proof and reader stacks now read `image:tag@sha256:<digest>` (the digest of the multi-arch index, so linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 both resolve) and keep their human-readable tag. A new static test, `scripts/ci/tests/test_image_digest_pins.py`, fails when a Dockerfile `FROM`, a Compose `image:` or a workflow container image has no digest; the few references that cannot carry one (images built in the same stack, build-arg bases, the release Dockerfiles until their follow-up change, the Go builder image) are listed with a reason in `scripts/ci/image_pins_allowlist.txt`, and a stale entry fails the test.
* SECURITY: **Dependabot now keeps every dependency ecosystem in the repository updated (CI and test tooling only; no change to any dependency version or to runtime behaviour).** `.github/dependabot.yml` gains `pip` (the hashed requirements locks, including the workflow linter's), `npm` (the documentation site and the Playwright proof project), `docker` (the deployment, MinIO build and S3 compatibility directories) and `docker-compose` (the benchmark, parity and external-reader stacks) entries next to the existing Go modules, GitHub Actions and root Dockerfile entries. Every entry runs weekly, waits 7 days before it proposes a new release, and groups minor and patch updates into one pull request per ecosystem; images this repository builds itself, the VictoriaLogs and VictoriaTraces pins and the test backend that the S3 compatibility job also pins are not proposed. `scripts/ci/tests/test_dependabot_coverage.py` fails when a tracked manifest directory has no matching entry or an entry has no schedule or cooldown, and the exceptions are listed with their reason in `scripts/ci/dependabot_allowlist.txt`. The `dependabot-cooldown` baseline entry is removed from `.github/zizmor.yml`.
* SECURITY: **The changelog gate no longer asks for an entry on Dependabot pull requests that only bump dependency files of the tooling and test trees (CI only; no change to any dependency version or to runtime behaviour).** `changelog-check` skips a pull request only when all of these hold: the event's author is `dependabot[bot]` and the head branch lives in this repository (not a fork), so a branch name, title or commit author cannot claim it; every changed file is modified, not added, deleted or renamed; and every file is a requirements file or hashed lock, a `package.json` or `package-lock.json` under `website/` or `tests/`, a Dockerfile or Compose file under `deployment/`, `scripts/` or `tests/` (including the S3 compatibility stacks), or a workflow in which only SHA-pinned `uses:` lines change. Anything else a Dependabot pull request touches (the Go modules, the release Dockerfiles `Dockerfile.logs`, `Dockerfile.traces` and `Dockerfile.datagen`, `charts/`, `cmd/`, `internal/`, `lakehouse-traces/`, `patches/`, `CHANGELOG.md`) keeps the existing rules, and the check fails closed when the author, the repository or the diff cannot be read. The gate script reads the author and repositories from the workflow's environment instead of interpolating them into the script, and `scripts/ci/tests/test_check_changelog_pr.py` covers the exempt cases, the human and spoofed-author cases and every file class that stays required.
